_meta.indication: Ranexa is indicated for the treatment of chronic angina; because it prolongs the QT interval, it should be reserved for patients who have not achieved an adequate response with other antianginal drugs.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, stratified, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of ranolazine SR 750 mg bid, 1000 mg bid, or placebo on background amlodipine, atenolol, or diltiazem.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with stable exertional (chronic) angina on background anti-anginal therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Exercise treadmill test (ETT) duration at trough.
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant increase in exercise duration vs placebo at trough: 750 mg +23.7 sec (p=0.030) and 1000 mg +24.0 sec (p=0.029).

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal study (only pivotal study in the resubmission)
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled parallel-group study adding ranolazine or placebo to amlodipine 10 mg daily in patients with at least 3 weekly angina attacks.
pivotal_trials.population: Angina patients with at least 3 average weekly angina attacks despite at least 14 days of amlodipine 10 mg daily.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Average weekly rate of angina attacks.
pivotal_trials.n: 565 randomized (Placebo N=281, Ranolazine N=277 in full analysis set)
pivotal_trials.result: Median weekly angina attacks during 6-week treatment phase 2.18 with ranolazine vs 2.43 with placebo (p=0.028).

key_safety: Most frequently reported treatment-emergent adverse events (>4%) occurring more often with ranolazine than placebo: dizziness (6.2%), headache (5.5%), constipation (4.5%), and nausea (4.4%). The principal safety concern is dose/concentration-related QTc interval prolongation, which has been associated with torsades de pointes and sudden death for other drugs.
target_moa: Antianginal/anti-ischemic agent whose precise mechanism is unknown; the sponsor claims ranolazine inhibits the late sodium current (INa) in myocytes, reducing intracellular sodium and calcium overload, with effects that do not depend on reductions in heart rate or blood pressure.

advisory_committee.vote: Ranolazine was the subject of the December 9, 2003 Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee meeting; no numerical vote tally is recorded in the medical review.

description.text: Changed Ranexa from second-line to first-line treatment for chronic stable angina

citations.quote: This efficacy supplement proposes to change the use of Ranexa® from second-line to first-line of treatment for patients with chronic stable angina. The sponsor submitted the results of protocol CVT 3036 in the defense of this application.

summary.text: Ranexa was approved via the standard 505(b) NDA pathway for treatment of chronic angina; the original application received an October 30, 2003 approvable letter and ranolazine was the subject of the December 9, 2003 Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee meeting, after which the sponsor generated additional data (ERICA/CVT 3037) and resubmitted on July 26, 2005, leading to approval with a renal-impairment pharmacokinetic postmarketing commitment.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Ranexa (ranolazine) 500 mg Extended-Release Tablets for the treatment of chronic angina.
Your July 26, 2005 submission constituted a complete response to our October 30, 2003 approvable letter.

A new drug application (NDA 21-526) was submitted for ranolazine on December 27, 2002 and a 4-month Safety Update was submitted on April 28, 2003. The Agency issued an approvable letter for ranolazine on October 30, 2003 and ranolazine was subsequently the subject of the December 9, 2003 Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee meeting.

requirement.text: Better define the impact of renal impairment on ranolazine exposure by re-doing the population pharmacokinetics using the entire database including patients with renal impairment; report due to the Agency by July 27, 2006.

citations.quote: The impact of renal impairment on exposure to ranolazine should be better defined. One way of achieving this would be to re-do the population pharmacokinetics of ranolazine using the entire database available including patients with renal impairment. The report of the re-analysis should be submitted to the Agency by July 27, 2006.

requirement.text: Alternatively, perform a new pharmacokinetic study in patients with different degrees of renal impairment, with the report submitted to the Agency by January 2008.

citations.quote: Alternatively, a new pharmacokinetic study should be performed in patients with different degrees of renal impairment. The report of this study should be submitted to the Agency by January 2008.
The Agency issued an approvable letter for ranolazine on October 30, 2003 and ranolazine was subsequently the subject of the December 9, 2003 Cardio-Renal Advisory Committee meeting.

basis.text: Deficiencies included delayed cardiac repolarization (QT prolongation) without a clear offsetting benefit given available alternative antianginals, inadequate safety exposure (fewer than 1000 patients given relevant doses for at least one month), and potential testicular toxicity (later resolved).

citations.quote: 1) Potential testicular toxicity, manifest as impaired fertility in rats in study AT-4136116-R-86-43285-PO-RMF. (This issue was later resolved per Agency meeting minutes, April 16, 2004).2) Delayed cardiac repolarization, manifest clinically as prolongation of the QT interval.

3) Adequate safety exposure. The database had information on fewer than 1000 patients given relevant doses of ranolazine for at least one month, an exposure well below what is typically expected for a chronic treatment for a symptomatic claim.
